verdicts.note: Title asked for both the states and what moves between them but the answer line gave only states; title narrowed to the states. Also used 'scheduler' before it is taught; now glossed inline.
Left out that strace pads spaces before '=' and that, on a terminal, the program's own output lands in the middle of the strace line; both added.
errno called a 'global variable'; it is a thread-local macro in practice, reworded.
Divide by zero does not trap on RISC-V, the profession's ISA; now says integer divide by zero on x86.
Data-race definition omitted 'non-atomic', so it would also cover correct atomic code; added.
amoadd.w is the 32-bit form but the card assumes a 64-bit atomic_long; now names lock xadd (x86) and amoadd generally.
Worked example was wrong: C2 was said to be waiting yet to take the item before C1 woke. C2 now arrives fresh and takes the item.
Unnamed POSIX semaphores do not work on macOS and the card named no platform; now says On Linux.
Said 'sometimes' prints parent first; with the initial value 1 the order is simply not guaranteed, reworded to 'can'.
Atomicity fix was incomplete: the thread that sets the pointer to NULL must take the same lock too; added.

summary.note: All 22 code snippets compiled and run or compile-checked on this Mac; outputs match (racy counter ~1.0M at -O0, atomic and mutex 2000000, TSan data race warning, segfault 139). Arithmetic in scheduling, time-slice, UART and event-loop cards re-derived. strace and semaphore behaviour from man pages.
